builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EdgePace: Deadline- and Freshness-Aware LLM Scheduling on Unified-Memory Platforms
summary: EdgePace replaces unmanaged LLM inference on unified-memory edge platforms (Jetson-class devices, smartphones) with a runtime that introduces safe suspension points across prefill and decode and schedules work by contention risk, deadline slack, and freshness. The cost is a custom runtime integrated into the inference stack, up to roughly 35% LLM throughput loss in the worst reported case, and applicability limited to unified-memory platforms with concurrent foreground sensor workloads. It can fail when foreground bandwidth demand is unpredictable enough to leave no safe scheduling window, when the portability work for a given inference engine is not done, or on discrete-GPU servers where memory contention is not the binding constraint.
rationale: The method targets real-time edge co-location of sensor pipelines and LLM inference, which is outside the reader's single-GPU/API production context, so it is worth tracking but not adopting or testing now.
technique: Bandwidth-Aware LLM Scheduling for Unified Memory

claims.statement: EdgePace replaces unmanaged LLM inference on unified-memory edge platforms (Jetson-class devices, smartphones) with a runtime that introduces safe suspension points across prefill and decode and schedules work by contention risk, deadline slack, and freshness. The cost is a custom runtime integrated into the inference stack, up to roughly 35% LLM throughput loss in the worst reported case, and applicability limited to unified-memory platforms with concurrent foreground sensor workloads. It can fail when foreground bandwidth demand is unpredictable enough to leave no safe scheduling window, when the portability work for a given inference engine is not done, or on discrete-GPU servers where memory contention is not the binding constraint.
Reduces foreground deadline misses by 24.1%--96.1% while retaining 64.9%--98.5% of LLM throughput; all measured LLM outputs arrive within task-defined freshness windows.
